metaDesc: AXEM-SX is a sovereignty-oriented Linux workstation OS built on openSUSE Leap 16.0 — a restrained environment for sustained, serious work.
heroSub: A sovereignty-oriented workstation operating system. Built for builders, architects, engineers, and long-cycle thinkers who require an environment that respects their attention and data sovereignty.
s1p1: Most operating systems try to disappear — becoming a frictionless void of abstract glass and transparency. AXEM-SX takes the opposite approach. We believe a workstation should feel like a place.
s1p2: Welcome to AXEM-SX 0.9 (Founders Preview). Built on the enterprise-grade foundation of openSUSE Leap 16.0, AXEM-SX is a purpose-driven workstation OS designed for disciplined productivity, sovereignty, and long-cycle reliability.
s1quote: Built on openSUSE Leap 16.0. A restrained Linux environment for sustained, serious work.
s2p1: In an era where software interfaces are increasingly abstract, flat, and detached, AXEM-SX reintroduces material metaphors.
s2p2: The Wood & Gold interface is not merely a theme — it is a signal of equilibrium. The wood textures remind the user that computing is a human activity rooted in the physical world. This grounded aesthetic is designed to reduce digital fatigue.
s2p3: Just as a carpenter respects their workbench, AXEM-SX respects your screen as a space for craftsmanship, not consumption.
s2card1Desc: Windows snap instantly. Transitions are minimized to reduce cognitive load.
s2card2Desc: Text and active elements prioritized for readability during long sessions.
s2card3Desc: Rapid navigation without mouse dependency — optimized for efficiency.
s3intro: AXEM-SX is built around three uncompromisable pillars:
s3pillar1Desc: Your data never leaves your machine. The AI runs locally. No remote services are pre-enabled. No "phone home."
s3pillar2Desc: The interface is designed to support focus — not fragmentation. Every default is intentional.
s3pillar3Desc: Built on Leap 16.0, supported until July 2034. Plan your long-term projects without forced obsolescence.
s4intro: AXEM-SX is not for everyone — and that is by design.
s4item1: Builders and makers who treat their workstation as a primary tool
s4item2: Architects and engineers who need long-cycle stability
s4item3: Creators who value independence over convenience
s4item4: Those who reject data exfiltration as a price for productivity
s4item5: Linux users ready to move beyond the general-purpose distribution
s5intro: AXEM-SX is committed to digital inclusion. The Digital Workshop must be accessible in the languages of those who need it most.
s5note: Note: Haitian Creole localization is a deliberate statement of digital inclusion — breaking away from the standard FIGS localization found in most Linux distributions.
